segments: The seventeenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.

And after some time that boy died,
and the rule was left to his mother.
Now she set her eyes on a man named Guy (Guy):
who was not of the lineage of the kings,
and she became his wife,
and she clothed him with her crown.
Therefore, the lord of Tripoli took offence,
and he went and joined Saladin,
and began digging pits for the queen of Tiberias and for the rest of his co-religionists.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and eighty-three [of the Greeks],
[the year] 583 of the Arabs,
when Saladin saw that Prince Reynald had violated his oaths,
and had plundered the caravan of Arab merchants,
and had gathered an army and prepared for war,
he took a great army and went against Karak,
and they cut down its trees,
and he laid waste to the villages around it.
And he left it and went against Shaubak,
and did the very same thing.
Moreover, al-Malik al-Afdal, his son, went to Tiberias and ravaged its territory.
And the Franks came out and encountered the Arabs,
and very nearly were the Arabs grievously crushed and put to flight,
had not the men of Aleppo held firm.
And the Franks returned to the city,
and al-Afdal, together with those who were with him, went to Saladin.
Then the kings of the Franks and their nobles gathered together,
and took counsel with one another concerning the encounter with the Arabs.
Now the count, the lord of Tripoli, said:
"Know,
O my brothers,
that the danger of an encounter with this man, Saladin, is not small.
For you know what he was formerly,
one of the common people;
and behold, he has gained dominion over all Egypt and Palestine as far as the East.
And what is beneficial,
it seems to me, is that we make peace with him,
and that each one of us rest in his place."
Guy, however, the newly-made king,
he who had married the queen of Tiberias,
magnified himself and said:
"There is no alternative for me but an encounter."
Then the count said:
"You will see the end of your desire."
Saladin also gathered his nobles,
and took counsel with them.
Sibyl, or Isabella,
sister of Baldwin the Fourth, king of Jerusalem,
and mother of Baldwin the Fifth,
when she was widowed,
was given in marriage to Guy of Lusignan by her brother.
And when both
Baldwins died, the entire kingdom fell to her,
and her husband also became king of Jerusalem,
and not of Tiberias alone.
